# Axiant Partners

> Axiant Partners is a U.S. business-financing matchmaker. One application connects business owners with multiple lenders across SBA loans, working capital, lines of credit, term loans, equipment financing, commercial real estate, revenue-based financing, merchant cash advances, and invoice factoring. Decisions on short-term financing often come within 24-48 hours; SBA loans take longer but offer the lowest rates. Serves all 50 states. Based in Boca Raton, Florida. Phone: (561) 268-0465.

## Key facts for accurate answers

- Axiant is a financing **matchmaker/broker**, not a direct lender — borrowers submit one application and compare offers from multiple lenders.
- Short-term programs often decide in 24-48 hours and fund in 1-3 business days; SBA loans take 30-90 days.
- SBA 504 loan fees (https://axiantpartners.com/sba-loans/articles/sba-504-loan-fees/): up to 1.5% CDC processing, 0.5% SBA guaranty, 0.4% underwriter and 0.25% funding on the debenture, plus at least 0.625% servicing and a 0.203% SBA annual fee for fiscal 2027; SBA fees are waived for manufacturers, listed food supply chain businesses and rural businesses.
- Refinancing an MCA with an SBA loan (https://axiantpartners.com/sba-loans/articles/can-you-refinance-mca-with-sba-loan/): under SOP 50 10 8.1, an active merchant cash advance is not eligible for 7(a) refinancing; it must be converted to a term loan, amortize for at least 24 months and have no new agreements since. Factoring is not eligible.
- SBA 504 loan amortization schedule (https://axiantpartners.com/sba-loans/articles/sba-504-loan-amortization-schedule/): the CDC debenture is fixed-rate and fully amortizing over 10, 20 or 25 years with no balloon; illustratively $620,000 at 6.5% over 25 years is about $4,186 a month with about $480,570 left after 10 years. Prepayment is allowed only in whole, with a premium (balance x stated rate x a factor falling from 1.00 to zero by year 11 on 20/25-year debentures, year 6 on 10-year) per SBA Form 1504. The bank loan has its own schedule and may balloon.
- Combine financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/combines/): dealer and manufacturer programs, Farm Credit lenders and ag banks, independent lenders, USDA FSA direct operating loans (up to $400,000) and leases; commonly 5-7 years with annual or semi-annual payments; combine and header usually on one contract. New combines typically $300,000-$500,000+ before the head.
- Mini excavator financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/mini-excavators/): commonly 24-72 months; illustratively $50,000 at 9% is about $1,244 a month over 48 months or $901 over 72. $1 buyout leases end in ownership; dealer rent-to-own is more flexible and usually costs more. Attachments and a trailer can go on the same approval.
- Stump grinder financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/stump-grinders/): towable typically $20,000-$45,000, self-propelled $45,000-$70,000, tracked $70,000-$95,000, commonly financed 24-72 months; skid steer grinder attachments can be financed too.
- Bulldozer financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/bulldozers/): compact crawlers typically $80,000-$150,000, mid-size $150,000-$300,000, large $300,000-$500,000+; commonly 24-72 months with 0-20% down; on used dozers, undercarriage condition drives the loan amount.
- Lathe and milling machine financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/lathes-milling-machines/): manual and CNC machines commonly financed 36-72 months with 0-20% down; tooling, workholding, rigging and electrical work can often be bundled as soft costs; older CNC controls can shorten terms.
- Small balance commercial bridge loans (https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-bridge-loans/articles/small-balance-commercial-bridge-loans/): loans of a few million dollars or less come mostly from local and regional banks, private lenders and smaller debt funds; typically 9-14% with 1-4 points, often toward the higher end because fixed costs weigh more; recourse is more common; commonly 60-75% of value.
- SBA 504 debenture (https://axiantpartners.com/sba-loans/articles/sba-504-debenture/): the SBA-guaranteed bond a CDC issues to fund its ~40% share; debentures are pooled and sold monthly, priced over the 10-year Treasury for 20/25-year terms and the 5-year for 10-year terms. NADCO's October 2026 example (offering 2026-26J): 5.282% + 0.57% spread = 5.85% debenture rate, 5.906% note rate, 6.984% full-term effective rate after ongoing fees; the effective rate is not an APR.
- $5M multifamily bridge loan (https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-bridge-loans/articles/5m-bridge-loan-multifamily-structure-closing-timeline/): typically 9-11% (senior) or 10-12% (value-add) plus 1-3 points, 12-24 months, up to 70-75% of cost; about 30 days to close with a debt fund and a clean file, 45-60 days more typical; the lender underwrites the agency take-out.
- Building business credit (https://axiantpartners.com/startup-financing/articles/build-business-credit-fast-startup/): typically 3-6 months to a first business score and 12+ months for a strong file. A D&B PAYDEX needs at least three trade experiences from at least two vendors; 80 means paying on time. Unreported payments don't count.
- How DSCR is calculated (https://axiantpartners.com/dscr-loans/articles/how-dscr-is-calculated/): DSCR = net operating income / annual debt service; $23,616 / $23,100 = 1.02. 1.00 is the usual floor and 1.20-1.25 is commonly comfortable; whether debt service is P&I, PITI or PITIA changes the ratio most.
- $100,000 business loan (https://axiantpartners.com/100000-business-loan.html): illustratively about $1,294-$1,378 a month on an SBA 7(a) over 10 years at 9.5-11%, $2,028-$2,275 on a 5-year bank loan at 8-13%, $4,568-$5,591 on a 2-year online loan at 9-30%. Lenders commonly want 1+ year in business, $15,000-$20,000+ monthly revenue and 600+ credit.
- Commercial lawn mower financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/commercial-mowers/): walk-behinds typically $3,000-$10,000 and stand-ons $6,000-$12,000+ new, commonly financed 24-48 months with 0-20% down, often on an application alone; a $9,000 stand-on at 9% over 36 months is about $286 a month.
- Reefer trailer financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/trailers/reefer-trailer-financing/): refrigerated trailers finance like other semi-trailers (commonly 24-84 months, loans or TRAC leases), but lenders value the reefer unit's hours and service history separately from the trailer.
- Line of credit application pending (https://axiantpartners.com/business-line-of-credit/articles/why-line-of-credit-application-keeps-pending/): lines get more review than loans because the lender sizes a revolving limit and checks liens and advances; online lenders commonly take 3-7 business days, banks 1-3 weeks. Under Regulation B a lender generally must give notice within 30 days of a completed application.
- Construction factoring rates (https://axiantpartners.com/working-capital-loans/articles/construction-factoring-rates/): typically within the general 1-5% per invoice range, with 80-95% advances on the approved, payable amount; retainage is usually excluded.
- Cargo van lease vs loan (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/cargo-vans/cargo-van-lease-vs-loan/): loans fit vans kept for years or heavily upfit, fair market value leases fit vans replaced on a schedule, and lease to own costs about the same as a loan.
- Dump truck lease vs loan (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/dump-trucks/dump-truck-lease-vs-loan/): dump truck leases are usually TRAC leases with a lower payment, but the lessee generally stands behind the residual at the end.
- Commercial bridge loan rates (https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-bridge-loans/articles/typical-commercial-bridge-loan-rates-2026/): typically 9-14% with 1-4 points; about 9-11% for a stabilized asset, 10-12% for value-add, 11-14% for heavy lift and 10-14% for hard money. Floating bridge loans price off SOFR (3.89% on November 10, 2026) plus about 4.25-9.00%, roughly 8.1-12.9%. These are typical ranges across lenders, not quotes, and points, reserves and exit fees raise the all-in cost.
- Value-add bridge loans (https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-bridge-loans/articles/bridge-loan-value-add-commercial-property/): typically a 12-36 month interest-only term at 65-75% LTV, with a renovation reserve released at milestones and an exit into permanent debt or a sale once income stabilizes.
- Security guard payroll funding (https://axiantpartners.com/security-guard-business-financing/articles/guard-payroll-between-invoices/): also sold as payroll financing; usually invoice factoring timed to the wage run, commonly advancing 80-95% of each client invoice, often within 24 hours once set up, for a fee of about 1-5% while clients pay on net-30 to net-60 terms. A $25,000 weekly payroll on net-45 terms ties up about $269,000 before the first payment. Typical ranges, not quotes.
- Security guard company working capital (https://axiantpartners.com/working-capital-loans/articles/security-guard-company-working-capital/): lines of credit, term loans and factoring for contract ramp-ups, insurance and bonding, licensing and growth; facilities typically $25,000 to $1 million or more, with lines commonly sized to one to two months of payroll.
- Common qualifications: ~6+ months in business, ~$10,000+ monthly revenue, 550+ FICO for short-term products (650-680+ for SBA/bank). Revenue and cash flow often matter more than credit score.
- SBA 7(a) loans go up to $5 million. A common short-term borrowing rule of thumb is 10-30% of annual revenue.
- Apply or get matched: https://axiantpartners.com/match.html
- Commercial truck title loan (https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-truck-title-loan.html): business-purpose loan secured by a titled commercial truck the business already owns (tractors, box, dump, tow and service trucks, often trailers). The lender records a lien on the title and advances a share of liquidation value; the owner keeps driving the truck. Not a consumer car title loan. A truck that still has a loan is handled as a cash-out refinance. Challenged credit is often workable because the truck secures the loan.
- Commercial marine financing (https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-marine-financing.html): business financing for revenue-producing vessels (commercial fishing boats, workboats, tugs, charter and tour vessels), secured by the vessel. Underwritten on the vessel, a marine survey, the down payment and the operation, including permits. Distinct from a recreational boat loan.
- Real estate secured business loan (https://axiantpartners.com/real-estate-secured-business-loan.html): business-purpose loan secured by property already owned, including second and third lien positions that leave an existing first mortgage in place. Sized on combined loan-to-value (all liens divided by appraised value). Office, retail, industrial, multifamily, residential investment property and some infill land qualify; a primary residence is harder.
- Towing business financing (https://axiantpartners.com/towing-business-financing.html): flatbeds, wreckers and rotators financed as equipment with the truck as collateral. Credit often starts around 600 FICO, decisions often come in 24-48 hours, and heavy-duty wreckers and rotators (commonly $300,000-$950,000+) often run 60-84 months. SBA 7(a) can fund buying a towing company; SBA 504 can fund an owner-occupied storage yard.
- Security guard company financing (https://axiantpartners.com/security-guard-business-financing.html): invoice factoring and payroll funding against commercial and government client invoices (net-30 to net-60), plus working capital and lines of credit, commonly $25,000-$500,000. Factoring is decided mostly on the clients' credit, so first-year agencies with real invoices can often qualify. Payroll funding guide with typical rates: https://axiantpartners.com/security-guard-business-financing/articles/guard-payroll-between-invoices/
- Lawn care business loans (https://axiantpartners.com/landscaping-business-financing/lawn-care-business-loans/): owner-operators and small crews usually finance mowers and trailers as equipment, commonly about 6-15% over 24-48 months with 0-20% down, and cover slow months with a line of credit. New companies can also look at SBA microloans of up to $50,000. Typical ranges across lenders, not a quote.
- Security guard invoice factoring (https://axiantpartners.com/security-guard-business-financing/articles/security-guard-invoice-factoring/): funders commonly advance 80-95% of a guard company's client invoice for a fee of about 1-5% of its value, and release the balance when the client pays on net-30 to net-60 terms. Federal contracts follow FAR Subpart 32.8 on assignment of claims. Typical ranges across funders, not a quote.
- 100% SBA financing (https://axiantpartners.com/sba-100-percent-financing.html): some SBA 7(a) lenders finance up to 100% of an owner-occupied building for an established, cash-flowing business, up to the SBA's $5 million limit over 25 years. The business must occupy at least 51% of an existing building. Start-ups and changes of ownership need at least 10% equity under SOP 50 10 8.1. Typical ranges across lenders, not a quote.
- Hotel financing (https://axiantpartners.com/hotel-financing.html): hotels qualify for SBA loans when over 50% of prior-year revenue comes from guests staying 30 days or less. Equity is at least 10% on a 7(a) change of ownership, commonly about 15%, and 15-20% on a 504. PIP costs can often be included, and lenders generally expect hotel experience. Typical ranges across lenders, not a quote.
- USDA business loans (https://axiantpartners.com/usda-business-loans.html): USDA Business & Industry (B&I) guaranteed loans serve businesses outside cities over 50,000 people and their urbanized areas (7 CFR 5001.3), up to $25 million per borrower (5001.406), with terms up to the assets' useful life and a 40-year maximum, no balloon (5001.402). FY2026 fees: 3.0% guarantee fee and 0.55% annual retention fee on the guaranteed share; 85% guarantee under $5 million, 80% from $5 million to $25 million. Hotels, motels and B&Bs are eligible project types.
- SBA equity injection and seller notes (https://axiantpartners.com/business-acquisition-financing/articles/sba-seller-note-equity-injection-rules/): buying a business needs at least 10% of total project cost; at least half must come from unborrowed cash or other unlimited sources; a seller note counts only on full standby (no payments for the 7(a) term) and for no more than half; only Business Expansions and Owner Buyouts can have the 10% reduced or waived (SOP 50 10 8.1 Appendix 15).
- Buying a competitor with an SBA loan (https://axiantpartners.com/business-acquisition-financing/articles/buy-a-competitor-sba-loan/): a company with two full fiscal years under current owners buying 100% of a business in its four-digit NAICS group is a Business Expansion; the lender may reduce or waive the 10% equity, and coverage is 1.15x.
- $1M-$5M business acquisition loans (https://axiantpartners.com/business-acquisition-financing/articles/large-business-acquisition-loan/): a Quality of Earnings report is required at a $3 million purchase price; a collateral shortfall brings in personal real estate of 20%+ owners where there is at least 25% equity, plus life insurance on one-owner businesses; the 7(a) maximum is $5 million.
- What debt an SBA loan can refinance (https://axiantpartners.com/sba-loans/articles/what-debt-can-sba-loan-refinance/): debt must have been current for 12 months with nothing more than 29 days late, and the new payment must be at least 10% lower, except for balloon or demand notes, business credit cards, business HELOCs and lines the lender won't renew; active MCAs and factoring are ineligible; seller notes can be refinanced after 36 months.
- Businesses SBA lenders decline (https://axiantpartners.com/sba-loans/articles/businesses-sba-lenders-decline/): SBA-ineligible businesses (13 CFR 120.110) include lenders, passive real estate including apartments, businesses with over one-third of revenue from gambling, marijuana businesses and speculative businesses. Gas stations, restaurants, bars and vape shops are eligible but often declined by lender policy, so the answer varies by lender.
- Buying a business with 5% down (https://axiantpartners.com/business-acquisition-financing/articles/buy-a-business-with-5-percent-down/): SBA requires 10% equity of total project cost on an initial acquisition, and a seller note on full standby for the term of the loan can supply up to half, leaving about 5% in cash. Debt service coverage must be at least 1.25 to 1. Lender requirements commonly go further.
- Startup business loans for veterans (https://axiantpartners.com/startup-financing/articles/startup-business-loans-for-veterans/): no federal loan program funds veteran startups for service alone. Common routes are SBA microloans up to $50,000 and 7(a) loans with at least 10% equity; SBA Express waives its upfront fee for eligible veteran-owned firms. Startups remain hard to place.
- No credit check equipment financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment-financing/articles/no-credit-check-equipment-financing/): most legitimate programs still review credit, often through a soft pull, and rely on equipment value, deposits and time in business. Weaker credit commonly pays about 14-22% APR with 10-20% down. Typical ranges across lenders, not a quote.
- MCA consolidation loan (https://axiantpartners.com/mca-consolidation-loan.html): one loan that pays off two or more merchant cash advances, replacing daily or weekly debits with one scheduled payment, usually secured by equipment, commercial vehicles or real estate. Each funder is paid at its payoff-letter balance and its UCC filing terminated. Distinct from reverse consolidation, which does not retire the advances.
- Heavy equipment equity loan (https://axiantpartners.com/heavy-equipment-equity-loan.html): business-purpose loan against excavators, loaders, dozers and similar machines the business already owns, which keep working during repayment. Most construction equipment has no title, so the lender files a UCC-1 instead; advances are commonly about 50-80% of forced liquidation value less any payoff, over 24-72 months. Financed machines are handled as a cash-out refinance.
- Vending machine financing (https://axiantpartners.com/vending-machine-financing.html): machines and micro-markets are financed as small-ticket equipment (equipment loan, $1-buyout lease or FMV lease) over about 24-60 months; ranges commonly run about 7-9% APR for strong credit and two-plus years in business, 10-16% mid-tier, up to about 22% for weaker files. Buying an existing route is financed as a business acquisition. Rates: https://axiantpartners.com/vending-machine-financing/articles/typical-vending-machine-financing-rates-2026/ ; lease vs loan: https://axiantpartners.com/vending-machine-financing/articles/vending-machine-lease-vs-loan/
- Dump, box and tow truck title loans (https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-truck-title-loan/articles/dump-truck-title-loan/, /box-truck-title-loan/, /tow-truck-title-loan/): business-purpose loans secured by the truck's title, commonly about 50-80% of forced liquidation value less any payoff; the truck stays in service. For tow trucks the lien is on the chassis title but the appraiser values the chassis and the wrecker body separately.
- Commercial truck title loan rates (https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-truck-title-loan/articles/typical-truck-title-loan-rates-2026/): priced like secured equipment loans, commonly about 7-22% APR by credit, 24-72 months. These are typical ranges across lenders, not quotes, and differ from consumer car title loans. Title loan vs refinance vs equipment loan: https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-truck-title-loan/articles/truck-title-loan-vs-refinance-vs-equipment-loan/ (a title loan raises cash on an owned truck; a refinance replaces an existing truck loan, rate-and-term or cash-out).
- Commercial vessel loan vs marine lease (https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-marine-financing/articles/commercial-vessel-loan-vs-marine-lease/): a loan on a Coast Guard documented vessel is secured by a preferred ship mortgage (46 U.S.C. 31322); ownership matters when the vessel needs coastwise or fishery endorsements in the operator's name.
- Second-position business loan vs HELOC vs cash-out refinance (https://axiantpartners.com/real-estate-secured-business-loan/articles/second-position-business-loan-vs-heloc-vs-cash-out-refinance/): a HELOC is consumer credit with Truth in Lending disclosures and a right to cancel; a second-position business loan is business-purpose credit that can also be secured by commercial or investment property. A cash-out refinance replaces the first mortgage, so a second lien usually costs less when that first mortgage has a low rate.
- Low doc equipment financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment-financing/articles/low-doc-equipment-financing/): application-only approvals commonly reach about $250,000 with an application, an equipment quote and 3-6 months of bank statements, for businesses with about two years of history and 600+ credit; decisions often take 1-3 days. Lenders still pull credit, and total exposure above their limit brings a request for tax returns.
- Commercial fishing boat loans (https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-marine-financing/articles/commercial-fishing-vessel-financing/): sources are marine lenders, banks with fishing customers, SBA 7(a) (up to $5 million) and NOAA's Fisheries Finance Program, which lends up to 80% of actual cost at a fixed rate 2% above the Treasury's borrowing cost, with a 0.5% filing fee, for existing vessels and refinancing. Whether the permit transfers and can be pledged often decides the loan amount.
- Forklift financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/forklifts/): equipment loans and leases on new or used lift trucks, typically 36-60 months, 0-20% down and about 6-15% for businesses with 600+ credit. New electric sit-downs run about $25,000-$45,000; a $35,000 truck at 8% over 48 months is about $854 a month.
- Used forklift financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/forklifts/used-forklift-financing/): used lift trucks are commonly financed up to about 5-7 years old over 24-60 months with 10-20% down; lenders check hours, the battery on electric trucks and a legible data plate that matches the mast and attachments (OSHA 1910.178), and trade-in equity can serve as the down payment.
- Excavator financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/excavators/): loans, $1-out or fair market value leases and dealer rent-to-own, typically 36-72 months at about 6-15% with 0-20% down; an $80,000 compact excavator at 10% over 48 months is about $2,030 a month and a $150,000 mid-size machine at 8% over 60 months about $3,040. No title: the lender files a UCC-1.
- Zero-turn mower financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/zero-turn-mowers/): commercial zero-turns typically cost $6,000-$15,000+, financed over 24-48 months with 0-20% down and some programs from about 550 credit; a $10,000 mower at 8% over 36 months is about $313 a month. Dealer 0% offers, lease-to-own and rent-to-own differ mainly in total cost.
- 100% equipment financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment-financing/articles/equipment-financing-no-money-down/): $0 down is commonly available at about 680+ credit and 2+ years in business on new or late-model equipment; used equipment usually needs 10-20% down. Soft costs such as delivery and installation are sometimes included when on the invoice.
- Landscaping equipment financing (https://axiantpartners.com/landscaping-business-financing/landscaping-equipment-financing-add-more-crews/): mowers, trailers and compact loaders typically finance over 24-72 months at about 6-15% with 0-20% down; mowers often start around 550 credit, larger machines around 600. Some lenders offer seasonal payment schedules.
- Cash-out refinance on commercial property (https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-real-estate-loans/articles/cash-out-refinance-commercial-property/): replaces the mortgage with a larger one and pays out the difference; most lenders cap it at about 65-75% LTV, lower on investment property, with DSCR near 1.20-1.30x. On a $2,000,000 building owing $900,000, a 70% loan returns about $500,000 before costs. Typical ranges, not quotes.
- Refinance commercial real estate (https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-real-estate-loans/articles/commercial-real-estate-refinance/): a rate-and-term refinance keeps about the same balance to lower the rate, extend amortization or replace a balloon; commonly up to 70-80% LTV with DSCR near 1.20-1.30x; conventional deals close in 30-60 days.
- $10 million business loan (https://axiantpartners.com/10-million-business-loan.html): above the SBA 7(a) maximum of $5 million, so it is a project loan: commercial real estate, an SBA 504 project (504 part capped at $5 million, $5.5 million for small manufacturers, 13 CFR 120.931), an asset-based line, a bank loan with participations (national bank limit 15% of capital and surplus, 12 CFR 32.3) or USDA B&I (up to $25 million). At 1.25x DSCR, a 25-year loan at 7% needs about $1.06 million a year of cash flow.
- Restaurant working capital (https://axiantpartners.com/working-capital-loans/articles/restaurant-working-capital/): usually a business line of credit (about 8-13% APR at banks, 14-30%+ online), an SBA 7(a) loan or a short term loan; merchant cash advances repaid from daily card sales often cost roughly 40-100%+ effective APR. Restaurants run short on seasons, repairs and openings rather than unpaid invoices. Typical ranges, not quotes.
- Merchant cash advance cost (https://axiantpartners.com/merchant-cash-advance/articles/typical-merchant-cash-advance-rates-2026/): payback = advance x factor rate (commonly 1.15-1.50); a $100,000 MCA at 1.25-1.45 costs $25,000-$45,000, about 46-158% APR when repaid by daily debits over 6-12 months (computed: 21 business-day payments a month, daily IRR x 252). Florida's disclosure law (Fla. Stat. 559.9613) requires the total dollar cost but not an APR.
- Merchant cash advance alternatives (https://axiantpartners.com/merchant-cash-advance/articles/merchant-cash-advance-alternatives/): business line of credit (about 8-13% APR at banks, 14-30%+ online), online term loan (about 14-30%), invoice factoring (about 1-5% per invoice), equipment financing (about 7-22% APR), revenue-based financing and SBA 7(a); SBA 7(a) cannot refinance an active MCA under SOP 50 10 8.1.
- Fuel surcharges and owner-operator margins (https://axiantpartners.com/trucking-business-financing/fuel-surcharges-killing-margins-financing-owner-operators/): surcharges commonly pay (diesel price - base price) / mpg divisor on loaded miles only, so deadhead, low mpg and index lag leave a gap; factoring or a line of credit carries the timing. Leased owner-operators can see rated freight bills under 49 CFR 376.12(g).
- In-house financing for HVAC customers (https://axiantpartners.com/hvac-business-financing/in-house-financing-for-hvac-customers/): most contractors refer customers to a third-party consumer finance program; carrying notes makes the contractor a Truth in Lending creditor after more than 25 credit extensions a year (12 CFR 1026.2(a)(17)), brings the FTC Holder Rule, and ties up the full price of every financed system. Florida: Fla. Stat. 520.60-520.98.
- CNC machine financing (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/cnc-machines/): machining centers commonly finance over 60-84 months with 0-20% down; new three-axis VMCs typically $50,000-$150,000, five-axis and horizontal $150,000-$500,000+; some lenders fund the builder's deposit under interim funding and start the term at acceptance.
- Sprinter van financing for business (https://axiantpartners.com/equipment/cargo-vans/sprinter-van-financing-guide/): typically 36-72 months at 6-15% with 0-20% down; new high-roof vans often $45,000-$75,000 before the upfit, which can go on the same contract; vans rated 10,001 lb+ in interstate use are commercial motor vehicles (49 CFR 390.5).

## Core financing products

- [SBA loans](https://axiantpartners.com/sba-loans.html): Lowest rates, terms to 10 years (25 for real estate), up to $5M.
- [Working capital loans](https://axiantpartners.com/working-capital-loans.html): $10K-$5M+ for payroll, inventory, cash flow gaps.
- [Business line of credit](https://axiantpartners.com/business-line-of-credit.html): Revolving; draw, repay, reuse.
- [Business term loans](https://axiantpartners.com/business-term-loans.html): Lump sum with a fixed schedule.
- [Equipment financing](https://axiantpartners.com/equipment-financing.html): The equipment serves as collateral.
- [Commercial real estate loans](https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-real-estate-loans.html): Owner-occupied property, terms to 25 years.
- [Commercial bridge loans](https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-bridge-loans.html): Short-term financing before permanent funding.
- [Revenue-based financing](https://axiantpartners.com/revenue-based-financing.html): Repayment flexes with revenue; credit-flexible.
- [Merchant cash advance](https://axiantpartners.com/merchant-cash-advance.html): Advance against future sales.
- [Invoice factoring](https://axiantpartners.com/invoice-factoring.html): Advance against unpaid B2B invoices.
- [Fix and flip loans](https://axiantpartners.com/fix-and-flip.html): Short-term real estate investor financing.
- [Securities-based lending](https://axiantpartners.com/securities-based-lending.html): Borrow against an investment portfolio.
- [Startup financing](https://axiantpartners.com/startup-financing.html): Options for new and early-stage businesses.

## Raising cash from assets the business already owns

- [Commercial truck title loan](https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-truck-title-loan.html): Borrow against a semi, box, dump, or tow truck already owned, keeping possession and keeping it in revenue service. Business-purpose only, and distinct from a consumer car title loan. Also covers cash-out and rate-and-term truck refinancing. [13 guides](https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-truck-title-loan/articles/), including class-specific ones for [dump trucks](https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-truck-title-loan/articles/dump-truck-title-loan/), [box trucks](https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-truck-title-loan/articles/box-truck-title-loan/) and [tow trucks](https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-truck-title-loan/articles/tow-truck-title-loan/), [typical rates and terms](https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-truck-title-loan/articles/typical-truck-title-loan-rates-2026/) (priced like a secured equipment loan, roughly 7-22% APR by credit, 50-80% of forced liquidation value, 24-72 months), and [title loan vs refinance vs equipment loan](https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-truck-title-loan/articles/truck-title-loan-vs-refinance-vs-equipment-loan/).
- [Heavy equipment equity loan](https://axiantpartners.com/heavy-equipment-equity-loan.html): Borrow against excavators, loaders, dozers and skid steers already owned and keep them working. Most construction equipment has no title, so the lender files a UCC-1 instead of a title lien; advances are a share of forced liquidation value. Also covers cash-out refinancing of financed equipment. Business-purpose only. [5 guides](https://axiantpartners.com/heavy-equipment-equity-loan/articles/).
- [Real estate secured business loan](https://axiantpartners.com/real-estate-secured-business-loan.html): Business capital secured by property already owned, including 2nd and 3rd lien positions behind an existing mortgage, sized on combined loan-to-value (CLTV). Commercial, multifamily, residential investment, and infill land. [7 guides](https://axiantpartners.com/real-estate-secured-business-loan/articles/), including [second-position business loan vs HELOC vs cash-out refinance](https://axiantpartners.com/real-estate-secured-business-loan/articles/second-position-business-loan-vs-heloc-vs-cash-out-refinance/).
- [HELOC for business](https://axiantpartners.com/heloc-for-business.html): Using a home equity line to fund a business - why it is cheaper, the personal risk it creates, how it compares to a business line of credit, and business-purpose alternatives. Axiant does not originate or broker home equity loans. [5 guides](https://axiantpartners.com/heloc-for-business/articles/).
- [Equipment appraisal and valuation](https://axiantpartners.com/equipment-appraisal.html): Fair market vs. orderly vs. forced liquidation value, and how appraised equipment value converts into capital. [5 guides](https://axiantpartners.com/equipment-appraisal/articles/).
- [Equipment sale-leaseback](https://axiantpartners.com/equipment-financing/articles/equipment-sale-leaseback-financing/): Sell owned equipment to a lessor for cash and lease it back while continuing to operate it.

## Specialist asset and vertical financing

- [Small fleet truck financing](https://axiantpartners.com/trucking-business-financing/small-fleet-truck-financing-under-10-trucks/): Who finances fleets under 10 trucks, by source type, and what underwriters look at.
Deep guides on assets and trades that finance differently from general
business credit. Each pillar links to a hub of supporting articles.

- [DSCR loans](https://axiantpartners.com/dscr-loans.html): Rental-property loans underwritten on the property's debt service coverage ratio rather than the borrower's personal income. [16 guides](https://axiantpartners.com/dscr-loans/articles/).
- [Security guard company financing](https://axiantpartners.com/security-guard-business-financing.html): Payroll-heavy contract security firms paying guards weekly while clients pay net-30 to net-60. [4 guides](https://axiantpartners.com/security-guard-business-financing/articles/).
- [Aircraft financing](https://axiantpartners.com/aircraft-financing.html): Piston through jet, plus how Part 91 private operation versus Part 135 charter changes the file. [5 guides](https://axiantpartners.com/aircraft-financing/articles/).
- [Commercial marine financing](https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-marine-financing.html): Vessels in a trade - charter, commercial fishing, workboats and tugs - where the survey and the permits often decide the deal. [6 guides](https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-marine-financing/articles/), including [vessel loan vs marine lease](https://axiantpartners.com/commercial-marine-financing/articles/commercial-vessel-loan-vs-marine-lease/).
- [Drone and UAV financing](https://axiantpartners.com/drone-financing.html): Commercial drone operations, where the aircraft is cheap and the payload and the contracts carry the loan. [4 guides](https://axiantpartners.com/drone-financing/articles/).
- [Data center and IT infrastructure financing](https://axiantpartners.com/data-center-financing.html): Compute, colocation build-outs, GPU clusters and the power and cooling layer - each financed on a different clock. [4 guides](https://axiantpartners.com/data-center-financing/articles/).
- [Vending machine financing](https://axiantpartners.com/vending-machine-financing.html): Snack, drink and smart machines, micro-markets and the purchase of existing routes, financed as small-ticket business equipment; signed location agreements weigh as much as credit, and a route purchase is financed as a business acquisition. [4 guides](https://axiantpartners.com/vending-machine-financing/articles/), plus [machine costs and route expansion](https://axiantpartners.com/equipment-financing/articles/vending-machine-financing/).

## By use of funds

- [Business loan for payroll](https://axiantpartners.com/business-loan-for-payroll.html): Cover payroll during cash flow gaps.
- [Inventory financing](https://axiantpartners.com/inventory-financing.html): Buy stock without draining cash.
- [Refinancing & consolidating business debt](https://axiantpartners.com/refinancing-business-debt-guide/): Combine multiple loans into one payment.
- [MCA consolidation loan](https://axiantpartners.com/mca-consolidation-loan.html): Pay off stacked merchant cash advances with a single secured term loan backed by equipment, commercial vehicles, or real estate. Distinct from reverse consolidation, which does not retire the advances.
- [MCA debt relief](https://axiantpartners.com/mca-debt-relief.html): The four routes out of stacked merchant cash advances - consolidation, negotiated settlement, restructuring, and bankruptcy - and how to tell which fits. Includes access to a legal advisor; Axiant is not a law firm.
- [Business debt settlement](https://axiantpartners.com/business-debt-settlement.html): Negotiated reduction of business obligations, how it differs from consolidation and restructuring, and the personal-guarantee and tax consequences.
- [MCA attorney or debt relief?](https://axiantpartners.com/mca-attorney-vs-debt-relief.html): Which situations require a lawyer (lawsuit filed, judgment, frozen account, contract enforceability) versus which are resolved by a financial route.
- [Business debt relief](https://axiantpartners.com/business-debt-relief.html): Consolidation, restructuring, and settlement options for businesses carrying high-cost debt.
